requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
I found no gaps.

**Obligations**
1. Every definition referenced by the subject or any contributed source contributes its complete fenced declaration, including the phrase option.
2. Definitions referenced by those definitions are included transitively.
3. The transitive set has no duplicates.
4. The transitive set does not fail to terminate on cycles.
5. When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same complete transitive definition set is supplied to the model.
6. That set is recorded before a submission is accepted.

**Implementation**
- **Initial set (1, 2):** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` builds the mandatory inputs and then calls `definition_inputs`. It passes the contributed inputs and `Some(&subject.text)`, so terms in both the subject text and the contributed sources are covered. Each resulting definition becomes an `InputSelector::Definition` and goes through `source_input`, which yields the full declaration input (the fenced text, including `:phrase:`).
- **Closure (2, 3, 4):** `definition_inputs` calls `src/terms.rs#fn[dependencies]`.
  - `direct_references` collects terms from the subject text and from the text of each input. It scans Rust comments, Markdown bodies, requirement bodies, and definition inputs.
  - `close_dependencies` expands the terms to a fixed point with a `visited` set. That set gives no duplicates and no endless loop on cycles. The result is a `BTreeSet`.
- **Additional reads (5, 6):** `src/authoring/tools.rs#fn[read]` calls `sources.additional_definitions`, which runs the same `definition_inputs` closure. It drops definitions that were already delivered or recorded. The definitions are added to the tool result and to `ToolDelivery.inputs`. Line-range reads get their definitions through `src/authoring/pages.rs#impl[ResultPages]/fn[deliver]`. In `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]`, delivered inputs go into `pending`. After the next response, `record_inputs(&pending)` runs before any submission is parsed or accepted.

**Tests**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` covers the initial set. The subject cites `terms.unit`, which references `terms.value`, and the test asserts exactly two definition inputs. It therefore covers direct and transitive inclusion and no duplicates.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms]` covers a term referenced by a contributed source.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]` covers the read-introduced dependency.
  - The definitions `terms.unit` and `terms.value` reference each other, which exercises the cycle.
  - It asserts each definition appears once, in the recorded evidence.
  - Each definition's text starts with `:::{definition}`, and its second line starts with `:phrase: `.
  - The second request contains the definition text and the first does not, so supply happens before the submission.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` and `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` cover definitions delivered with item reads, line-range reads, and paged reads.

All obligations are implemented and tested, and I saw no unspecified behavior.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
